extractedWith: tools/extract/extract.ps1 -Batch p5-audit -Manifest <scratch copy of allowlist.manifest.yaml with batch p5-audit> -Clean (staging %TEMP%/codelab-extract/p5-audit, outside the repo; scrub findings are expected before the rewrite; secret scan clean)
promotion: Each staged file was read as a reference and rewritten with starter names and structure; "target" is the repo file it informed, "stagedTarget" the path in the staging folder. Content is a rewrite, so the repo file hash differs from stagedSha256.

origins.note: Rewritten: capture before the save (modified and deleted rows) and completion after it (inserts with their database keys) kept; the rows now go to the kernel audit.AuditEntries through IAuditTrailWriter on the module context's connection, inside a transaction the writer opens when the caller has none (the source wrote them with a second, separate save). State is kept per context (ConditionalWeakTable) because one scoped interceptor serves every module context; TimeProvider and the starter IAuditContextAccessor (SYSTEM actor) replace the source's clock and user lookup; values are masked at write time. Left behind: the suppression scope and the source's logging.

Rewritten as AuditPlans: one cached plan per IEntityType with a per-property treatment (Recorded, Identifier, Masked, Excluded) instead of an exclusion set; precedence is attributes, binary, secret names, key/foreign-key identifiers, personal-data names. Left behind: the namespace and central type exclusion lists of the source.

Rewritten: flat invariant formatting kept (relaxed JSON encoding for Arabic), but enums are recorded as their integer (wire convention), binary is never recorded, masking goes through Codelab.Observability PiiMask, and the catch-all around ToString is dropped (standards: no swallowed failures).
Pattern only: the central list of sensitive property names became generic name-part conventions (secrets excluded, personal data masked) as a safety net under the attributes.

Pattern only: the source's product-specific PII key list is not carried; its rule (generic labels such as Name or Description stay readable, person data is masked) shaped the generic name parts and the PersonalDataKind attribute.
Rewritten in the kernel Domain with starter wording; class and property targets kept, joined by PersonalDataAttribute/PersonalDataKind.

Pattern only (the Restrict fix): the source mapped the history-to-request foreign key with Cascade; HasRecordHistory<TRecord, THistory>() maps it with Restrict (required FK, timeline index RecordId + At) and RecordHistoryMapping.EnsureRestrict refuses a module model whose history foreign key cascades or sets null.
